title: Card-stack sidebar + routing proposal (working notes)
content:
Context / why this doc exists:
- Follow-up to nav audits (Oct–Nov 2025). Current left-rail is crowded: too many top-level items, deep model/route duplication, and poor discoverability of operation modes (Hosted / Dedicated / Private).
- Goal: propose a composable, card-first sidebar and a small set of routing rules that reduce cognitive load, make space for future product lines (Optimize, Observability), and simplify permission scoping for RBAC.

Guiding principles:
1) Surface actions at the right scope (workspace / project / model) instead of duplicating lists for environment.
2) Compact vertical density with expandable "stacks" (card groups) so power users can see depth on hover and novices get a minimal surface.
3) Router-first design: make URLs reflect the card hierarchy and support deep-linking and shareable ephemeral routes.
4) Progressive disclosure of advanced tools (rollouts, tracing, cache stats).
5) Low-friction migration: keep core routes identical where possible to avoid breaking bookmarks.

Proposal overview (high level):
- Sidebar becomes a series of "stacks" (cards grouped by area). Each stack header lives in the left rail; clicking expands a panel with card tiles for sub-pages.
- Top-level stacks: Home, Workspaces, Models, Deployments, Observe, Optimize, Settings.
- Workspaces stack is the first-class object: workspace -> project -> environment.
- Models stack contains catalog (browse), pinned models, and model health (regressions).

Card/stack UX patterns (wireframe notes):
- Closed state (rail width 56px): stack icons only, tooltip on hover.
- Peek state (hover expand): an overlay panel shows up to 6 card tiles (2 columns) with short descriptions and badges (latency / errors).
- Open state (click): persistent subnav in a second column with full list, search/filter, and "quick actions" for each card (3-dot menu, deploy snapshot, open evals).
- Compact mode: collapse stacks to icons-only, preserve keyboard navigation (Ctrl+K to jump).

Routing rules (draft):
- Routes should be canonical and param-driven. Examples: 
  - /workspaces/:workspaceId/projects/:projectId -> project root
  - /workspaces/:workspaceId/projects/:projectId/environments/:envId/deployments/:deploymentId -> deployment details
  - /models/catalog -> model browser; /models/:modelId/versions/:versionId -> model detail
  - /observe/requests -> request inspector, /observe/requests/:requestId -> trace view

- Router behaviours to implement:
  - Stack-preserving navigation: when navigating within a stack, the stack remains open; deep-linking should also open the correct stack automatically.
  - Fallback mapping: unknown route -> try to resolve using last-known resource index (helps migrating old bookmarks).
  - Legacy aliases: map /api/console/* legacy routes to new canonical routes for 6 months.

Information architecture:
- New object-first hierarchy places Workspaces before Models and Deployments. Rationale: teams operate by workspace/project boundaries; models are resources used by those scopes.
- Search-first header: always-on global search with quick filters (by workspace, model, deployment). Search results support open-in-place (preview card) to avoid full navigation when possible.

Permissions and visibility notes:
- Stack-level permissions: a user may have visibility of a stack without access to all cards inside it. Example: read-only on Observe but no access to APM traces.
- Route-scoped entitlement checks implemented as route guards to reduce flicker.

Backlog grooming (candidate stories):
- RWI-1987: Implement card-stack component (ui-kit) - props: title, icon, badges, peekTiles (max 6) - 5d EPIC
- RWI-1988: Router behavior: auto-open stack for deep-links + legacy alias mapping - 3d
- RWI-1989: Workspaces index page (list + quick create) + migrate current workspace selector to left-rail - 4d
- RWI-1990: Peek overlay accessibility (keyboard only) + screenreader text - 2d
- RWI-1991: Permission matrix for stacks/cards (backend + route guards) - 6d
- RWI-1992: Telemetry events: stack_open, peek_tile_click, quick_action_trigger - 2d
- RWI-1993: Migration job to create redirect table for legacy links - 3d

Acceptance criteria (initial):
- All canonical routes resolve to the same resource as before (or redirect with 301/302 mapping).
- Stack peek works in Chrome/Firefox/Safari and is keyboard accessible.
- RBAC guards prevent rendering action buttons when a user lacks entitlement; page-level 403 handled gracefully (inline CTA to request access).
- No console errors during bulk navigation stress test (5000 simulated users hitting various routes).

Design notes / micro-interactions:
- Hover latency for peek overlay: 120ms delay to avoid accidental opens (experimentable param).
- Quick action affordances: small icon-only buttons in peek tiles; confirm modals only for destructive actions (delete/rollback).
- Breadcrumbs: keep, but make them tappable chips that can collapse into an ellipsis for long paths.
- Back-button behaviour: if pivoting between stacks, preserve previous stack open state in history entry.

Open questions / risks:
- Does moving Workspaces above Models break third-party integrations that assume model-first URLs? (Mitigation: strong legacy aliasing + deprecation timeline)
- Peek panel performance on large accounts (200+ models) — we should limit peek tiles to recent + pinned and rely on full open to paginate.
- How to represent cross-workspace resources (shared models) in this hierarchy? Proposed: shared models live in Models -> Shared; we surface pinned shared models in workspace peek.

Rollout plan (phased):
1) UI-kit component + router infra changes behind feature flag (canary tenants) - 3 weeks
2) Enable card-stack for internal teams + select beta customers (opt-in) - 2 weeks
3) Collect telemetry, iterate on peek delay and tile density - 2 weeks
4) Open to all hosted users, enable legacy alias redirects, announce migration - 1 week

Metrics to watch post-launch:
- Navigation success rate (click -> content load within SLO)
- Average time-to-target (keyboard/shortcut -> page)
- Bounce on root workspace page (should decrease)
- Support tickets referencing "can't find" routes (should decrease)
- Telemetry: peek_tile_click -> conversion to full open

Notes for engineers / follow-ups:
- Marco: pick the ui-kit token names for stack states (closed/peek/open) and add CSS vars for width/density.
- Priya: write e2e tests for deep-link auto-open behavior and legacy aliasing.
- Diego: coordinate with infra to add redirect table and a short-lived lookup API for legacy slugs.

Quick sketch (ASCII):
[left rail: icons]
[peek overlay]  [content area]
 Workspaces     | Workspace A | Project X | env: prod
  Models          | Model catalog (tile)  | pinned

TODO (near-term):
- Finalize stack names and order (stakeholder poll) - deadline 2026-02-22
- UX microcopy for peek (title + 1-line summary) - assign Priya
- Add migration docs for customer success (how to update bookmarks) - assign Diego

This is a working doc; please add inline notes or comments. I plan to lock a version and create a decision log when we pick the final ordering and rollout SLOs.
